punchline: According to Hill, Carnegie's edge wasn't knowing how to make steel. It was knowing who did and pointing them all at one goal.
thirty_sec: Andrew Carnegie arrived in America as a poor Scottish boy and worked ordinary jobs in a mill, a telegraph office and on the railroad. He went on to build one of the biggest steel businesses of his time, which became part of U.S. Steel in 1901. Napoleon Hill, who says Carnegie shared his secret with him, credits two things. The first was one definite purpose, steel, pursued relentlessly. The second was a 'Master Mind' of associates whose expertise Carnegie relied on instead of his own.
question: When a goal feels out of reach, is it really your skills holding you back, or the lack of one clear aim and the right people to chase it with?
